sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201].

The path was cyclical rather than smooth: a 20.4% jump in FY2018 to $54.7 billion [F3][D92], a 22.4% collapse in FY2020 to $41.7 billion [F5][D198], then a 12.8% rise in FY2023 to $67.1 billion [F8][D357].
The FY2020 decline came from lower sales volume driven by lower end-user demand and dealer inventory reductions across all three primary segments [P59].
The FY2023 gain was primarily favorable price realization and higher sales volume [P32], and operating margin rose 6.0pp that year to 19.3% [F28][D370].
In FY2025 Power & Energy contributed 5.2pp of the 4.3% revenue growth on 11.6% growth and a 47.6% share of revenue [D759][D463][D758][D757].
Total sales rose $2.780 billion in FY2025 on higher sales volume of $3.389 billion, partly offset by unfavorable price realization of $817 million [P13].
Construction Industries subtracted 0.6pp as sales fell 1.6% [D766][D765], and Resource Industries was flat at $12.5 billion [D779][S111].
Construction's decline was primarily unfavorable price realization of $1.136 billion, partly offset by higher sales volume of $568 million [P8].
Operating costs grew 4.8pp faster than revenue in FY2025 [D489], and operating income fell 14.7% against revenue growth of 4.3% [D464][D463].
Operating margin of 16.5% in FY2025 [F30] sat above the 14.3% window median but below the 20.2% FY2024 high [D1123][D1122].
The 3.7pp margin decline in FY2025 [D476] was primarily unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion and unfavorable price realization of $817 million, partly offset by higher sales volume [P9].
Cost of revenue accounted for -4.2pp of the FY2025 bridge, while SG&A and R&D were roughly neutral at -0.0pp and +0.1pp [D490][D492][D491].
In FY2025 net margin of 13.1% sat 3.4pp below the 16.5% operating margin [F50][F30], with a 24.0% effective tax rate [D449].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion was 1.32x net income in FY2025 [F80][F40][D450], and free cash flow of $8.9 billion was 1.00x [F100][D451].
Free cash flow margin of 13.2% [D447] was above the 11.9% window median but below the 16.8% FY2023 high [D1129][D1128].
Capex rose 41.9% to $2.8 billion, or 4.2% of revenue, and reached 1.25x D&A [F90][D470][D446][D452].
Machinery, Power & Energy operating cash flow rose to $12.278 billion primarily on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes paid [P4].
Net debt stood at $26.2 billion in FY2025, net cash of -38.8% of revenue [D456][D457].
That net cash level was above the -35.6% industrials peer median (n=7) but in the 43rd percentile [D1152][D1151].
Buybacks of $5.2 billion plus dividends of $2.7 billion were 89.0% of free cash flow [X140][X150][D459], and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D483].
Return on average equity of 43.5% was in the 100th percentile against a 23.3% peer median (n=6) [D462][D1155][D1156].
Net cash fell for a second year into net debt of $26.2 billion in FY2025 from $22.1 billion in FY2023 [D456][D350][R1].
Leverage is still modest against equity of $21.3 billion [F200], but the direction matters if tariffs keep pressuring manufacturing costs [P9].
Revenue fell 3.4% in FY2024 to $64.8 billion [F9][D410], the only decline since FY2020 [R2].
One down year after a record FY2023 is cyclical, not structural, given the FY2025 rebound [F10].
FY2021-FY2025 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and differs from the 10-K by up to 0.06% [R3][F40][X20].
The gap is immaterial to margins and cash conversion but should be noted where precision matters [R3].
Whether FY2026 operating margin holds above the 14.3% window median [D1123], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether capex stays above the 4.2% of revenue reached in FY2025 [D446], reported in the FY2026 cash flow statement.
Whether net cash as a share of revenue recovers from -38.8% [D457], reported in the FY2026 balance sheet.
